standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the graded bivariant groups A^p(X -> Y) and the Chow groups on which they act; the rest of the proof uses no other citation.

core_obligations: Construct a map from the product to the left hand side: given a family of classes c_i on the pieces, send a class beta on Y to the class on X whose restriction to each X_i is the cap of c_i with the restriction of beta to the corresponding Y_{a(i)}, noting that the Chow group of X is the product of the Chow groups of the X_i; repeat after an arbitrary locally finite type base change to obtain a bivariant class, giving a map Psi (proof lines 6636-6644).

Construct the inverse map: given a bivariant class c on X over Y and a class beta_i on Y_{a(i)}, take the restriction to X_i of the cap of c with the pushforward of beta_i along the open and closed immersion of Y_{a(i)} into Y, and again repeat after base change to obtain a class c_i on the piece, giving a map Phi (proof lines 6645-6651).

Check the two composites: the one composite is immediately the identity by inspection, and for the other one uses that a bivariant class commutes with flat pullback and with proper pushforward: restricting the cap of c with beta to the union of the pieces lying over a fixed Y_j equals the cap of c with the restriction of beta, and pushing that forward along the union map equals the cap of c with the pushforward of the restriction, which shows that the original class is recovered (proof lines 6652-6671).
proof_roadmap: Define the map from the product to the bivariant group and note it respects base change (proof lines 6636-6644).
Define the map in the opposite direction by restricting and pushing forward along the pieces (proof lines 6645-6651).
Verify the two composites using the flat pullback and proper pushforward compatibilities of a bivariant class (proof lines 6652-6671).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the bivariant group of a morphism of disjoint union decompositions as the product of the bivariant groups of the pieces, over an arbitrary index set (statement lines 6622-6634, tag 0FDZ). The proof builds both maps explicitly and then has to check the non-trivial composite: for a fixed piece of the target it uses that a bivariant class commutes with flat pullback to move the restriction of the cap into the pullback, and that it commutes with proper pushforward to identify the pushed forward restricted cap with the cap of the pushed forward class. Because the indices are arbitrary, the argument has to be phrased through the product decompositions of the Chow groups rather than finitely many cases, which is the substance, so the claim is H2.
